result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d make genuine understanding the default — not just information, but the willingness to see other perspectives, question our own assumptions, and bridge the gaps that fear and ignorance create.

So many of the world’s biggest problems — conflict, inequality, environmental destruction — are fueled by a failure to truly understand one another and the systems we’re part of. If people could step outside their own echo chambers and grasp the lived realities of others, we’d be far more likely to collaborate, compromise, and act with compassion.

Understanding doesn’t guarantee agreement, but it makes empathy possible. And empathy is the foundation for every meaningful change we could ever hope to make.
